    When does the Higgsfield Black Friday sale end?

    How do I use a Higgsfield promo code?

    Sign in, click your avatar, choose Manage Account, open Promocode in the left sidebar, select Enter code, and type the code exactly, with no extra spaces. Higgsfield says the benefit is applied instantly and the page then shows the discount and any credits added. One code means one activation unless its terms say otherwise. Promo credits expire on the date shown when they are added, and Support codes expire if they are not activated within 7 days. Source: How do promocodes work?, dated Aug 3, 2026.

    Where do real Higgsfield promo codes come from?

    From Higgsfield itself. Its help center names three sources: marketing promos announced on its official social media channels first, codes for active participants in Higgsfield Discord community events, and Support promos issued case by case, which cannot be requested. A code on a coupon site that does not appear on one of those channels is not listed here. Source: How do promocodes work?.

    Does the discount last after the first payment?

    No. Higgsfield’s help center says a promo price applies to the first payment or the period stated in the offer, and the plan then renews at the standard price. Its Nov 11, 2026 changelog says a sale discount covers the first year of an annual plan or the first month of a monthly one. The monthly cards say so directly, for example Plus at $47 “renews at $59.” For annual plans the sources disagree: the plan data the pricing page loads lists the annual discount as lasting “forever,” with a renewal price equal to the sale price. What an annual plan renews at after its first year is not confirmed. Sources: How do promo prices work?, dated Aug 1, 2026 · Higgsfield changelog, Nov 11, 2026. What each plan costs at its standard price is in Higgsfield pricing explained and is Higgsfield worth it?. To compare other tools by cost per second, see Higgsfield alternatives.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
